doc.title: Jerry Hey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 2, 2023

title: Producers' reactions to his parts and getting paid
summary: Producers hire him for what he has done before; he will change anything and has rarely gone unpaid.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Do you ever get over the moment of, I don’t know if anxiety is the right word, but the first time you’re reading down what you arranged and you’re in the studio and the producer is there and you’re waiting to hear the comment about your parts — or do they already know sort of what it’s going to sound like?

Well I don’t know if they, you know, really Quincy may, Foster may, but you know a lot of the other people that are more producers and less musician, you know they’re not necessarily, but the reason they hired me was because they liked what I’ve done in the past, so they know, I guess they’re assuming that it’s going to be what they’re looking

for. You know sometimes they’ll say, “You know I’m not really sure on that one.” And okay, what can I do to make it better? But anything that I write, I don’t care, it’s their record if they don’t like it I’ll change it.
Have you ever not gotten paid because they didn’t like your writing?
No. I’ve not gotten paid a couple of times because they were schmucks, but —
But yeah, no that’s kind of always upfront, this is how much it’s going to cost you, you know studio engineer, horns and arranging, okay, great.
